title: Murmuration — handoff mini-runbook (swing→night)
content:
Context:
- Quick notes for swing->night handoff. This is a lightweight, portable checklist for the next oncall to pick up fast. Not a full formal runbook; use the Confluence page for canonical procedures.

Top-of-shift summary:
- Cluster health: all regions GREEN except eu-west-1 (intermittent GPU eviction warnings on p3-preempt). We routed ~4% of production traffic to fallback-model-b for last 3 hours.
- Top alerts to watch: token-service-queue-latency (>150ms sustained), kv-cache-miss-rate (>12%), model-router-failures (spike at 02:10 UTC yesterday).
- Recent deploys: model-router v1.14.2 (canary) rolled to 10% — watch latency A/B. Autoscaler config change applied at 03:00 (shorter cooldown).

Immediate things I did / in-progress:
- Warmed up KV cache for prefix groups: billing-ledgers, chat-history, rerank-candidates (see commands below).
- Issued temporary routing policy RU-2026-03-10 to prefer low-latency pool for short queries (<128 tokens).
- Raised INF-4821 (Jira) to track repeated p3 eviction pattern; attached kernel logs and pod dumps.

Quick checklist for next shift:
1) Check the three dashboards: "Token latency by route", "KV cache hit/miss by keyspace", "Model router error breakdown".
2) If token latency > 180ms for >10min: rollback model-router canary to 0% (steps below).
3) If KV miss rate > 18% and mem pressure high: increase cache-resources on cache-prod-1 by +2Gi or clear the least-used prefix (prefetch after clearing).
4) If p3 eviction returns: drain any canary pods on that node and move traffic to dedicate-gpu-pool-b; open a ticket to infra team.

Useful commands (kubectl / internal tools):
- Tail token service logs: k -n inference logs -f deploy/token-service --since=2m
- KV cache metrics: curl -s http://metrics.internal/kv-cache?prefix=cache-prod-1 | jq .hit_rate
- Force warm cache for a prefix (unsafe, do during low traffic): /opt/bin/cache-warm --prefix billing-ledgers --concurrency 4 --ttl 3600
- Rollback router canary: infractl rollout set model-router --percent 0 --reason "latency rollback"
- Reroute traffic to fallback-model-b for route /chat: routerctl route set /chat --model fallback-model-b --until 2026-03-13T06:00Z

Temporary mitigation recipes (short-term):
- High token latency (caused by long KV lookups): add a short-circuit local cache on the ingress side for the hot prefix (see runbook snippet). Command: routerctl cache attach --route /write --prefix chat-history --size 50MB
- Repeated evictions on specific instance type: set node taint to avoid scheduling long-lived model pods: kubectl taint nodes <node> curated=avoid:NoSchedule (then cordon/evict).

Known quirks / gotchas:
- Model-router v1.14.2 introduces a small regression: when sequence length >2048 and batch-size auto-scaler triggers, the router sometimes sends downstream requests with missing KV token headers — watch for 400s with header "X-KV-Trace: missing".
- The autoscaler cooldown change (shortened) can thrash if traffic has sudden microbursts; if you see >3 scale events in 5m, flip cooldown back via infractl.
- Many dashboards time-shift metrics by 30 seconds; correlate with tracing if in doubt.

Open action items (todo):
- [ ] Attach full podcore for INF-4821 to the Jira before EOD. (Maya)
- [ ] Add a small synthetic load test for <128 token flows to validate fallback routing. (Ethan)
- [ ] Draft a tiny runbook snippet for ingress-side short-circuit caches and push to Confluence. (Me / next shift)

If you need to escalate:
- Pager escalation matrix: oncall -> sr-sre -> eng-cto. If customer-impacting, page product-support as well.
- For urgent infra-level evictions contact: ops-hardware@redwood (and call Ethan).

Notes-to-self (things I scribbled and didn't resolve):
- Why did the fallback-model-b produce 1.2% more hallucinations on route /qa? Add a small eval to repro with the exact prompt set.
- Consider lowering prefix eviction threshold for chat-history to 3h (currently 12h). Could reduce cold-start penalty.

Short contact map:
- Maya Chen — SRE (pager backup) — slack: @maya — mobile: 415-555-0182
- Ethan Brooks — infra eng — slack: @ethanb — mobile: 415-555-0127

If you pick this up, please ping me in the #infra-oncall thread and add short summary to the Jira comment so I can follow up tomorrow AM.

Versioning/where to find canonical: Confluence page for 'Prod inference runbooks' has the formal steps, this doc is temporary and lightweight.

End of notes.
